what_its_for: Darifenacin is used to treat an overactive bladder. It helps reduce the sudden urge to urinate, how often you need to urinate, and accidental leaking of urine (urge incontinence). It works by relaxing the bladder muscle so your bladder can hold more urine.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with a glass of water. Do NOT crush, chew, or split the tablet. You can take it with or without food. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 7.5 mg once daily. Your doctor may increase your dose to 15 mg once daily after 2 weeks if needed. Always follow the exact dose your doctor prescribed. Do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on that same day. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and just take your next regular dose. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store darifenacin at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you, as it may cause blurred vision or dizziness. Avoid becoming overheated or dehydrated, since this medication can reduce sweating and raise your body temperature. Limit or avoid alcohol, as it can increase dizziness. Tell your doctor about ALL other medicines you take, especially antifungals like ketoconazole, antibiotics like clarithromycin, and other bladder medicines, as they can interact with darifenacin.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: inability to urinate or very little urine output, severe stomach pain or bloating, signs of heat stroke (hot and dry skin, high fever, confusion), swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat (signs of allergic reaction), new or worsening eye pain or vision changes. Also call your doctor if you have worsening constipation, severe dry mouth, confusion, or if your bladder symptoms are not improving after a few weeks.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement in your bladder symptoms within the first 1 to 2 weeks of taking darifenacin. However, it may take up to 4 to 8 weeks to feel the full benefit of the medication. Keep taking it even if you do not notice immediate results.
special_populations: Older adults (age 65 and over): You may be more sensitive to side effects like confusion, constipation, dry mouth, and dizziness. Use with caution and report any unusual symptoms to your doctor. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: It is not known if darifenacin is safe during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Liver problems: If you have moderate liver disease, your dose should not exceed 7.5 mg per day. This medicine is NOT recommended if you have severe liver disease. Kidney problems: No dose adjustment is usually needed for kidney problems, but always inform your doctor about any kidney issues.
